Words: Brennan 先生。我听 Morrison 说，Gray 小姐去认罪了？
Mr. Brennan. I heard from Morrison that... Miss Gray went and confessed?
怎么？她替别人顶罪，正合了你们这些想明哲保身的人的意吧。
What, surprised? She's taking the fall for someone else... must be convenient for all you people trying to keep your heads down.
少拿 Gray 小姐来试探我，Brennan。该回答的我会回答，但别指望我替任何人表态。
Do not use Miss Gray to test me, Brennan. I will answer what I can, but do not expect me to declare myself for anyone.
那我们就来聊聊Webb的事。
Then let's talk about Webb.
没错。
That's right.

Parameters.ParameterStr: Webb 好像一直在一笔叫“鲸鱼”（Whale）的账上栽跟头。
Parameters.ParameterEn: Webb kept running into trouble over an account called Whale.

Parameters.ParameterStr: 看看这枚案发现场的弹壳。是不是让你想起了点旧伤？
Parameters.ParameterEn: Look at this casing from the crime scene. Does it bring back an old wound?

Words: Webb 好像一直在一个叫 Whale 的人身上栽跟头。
Webb kept tripping over someone called Whale.
你看他的字迹，写这名字的时候手都在抖。
Look at his handwriting here. His hand was shaking when he wrote this name.
……是他的字迹。
...That's his handwriting, all right.
这种大人物，总不能是坐在家里等收账吧。
A man like that doesn't just sit at home waiting for the money to roll in.
酒吧里来来往往这么多人，总得有双眼睛替他盯着这笔投资。
All those people coming and going through this bar... someone's got to be keeping an eye on his investment.
眼睛是有。不过，那些自以为掩饰得很好的眼睛，其实很明显。
There are eyes, sure enough. But the ones who think they're being subtle... they're usually the most obvious.
比如？
Such as?
比如最近常来找Webb先生的那位 Rita 小姐。
Such as that Miss Rita who's been coming around to see Mr. Webb lately.
她点马提尼，却从来不碰杯口。
She orders a martini every time... but never touches the rim of the glass.
反而总是盯着我们会客室那条走廊。
Instead, her eyes are always on the corridor leading to our meeting room.
每当 Webb 先生见完那些大主顾，她总会借故和他们攀谈，打听点什么东西。
Every time Mr. Webb finished meeting one of his big clients, she'd find some excuse to chat them up... fishing for something.
我干了这么多年，有些人的心思，不用问我也能看出来。
I've been doing this long enough. Some people's intentions... you don't need to ask to see them.
原来 Whale 的耳目早就坐在你们眼皮子底下了。
So Whale's eyes and ears have been sitting right under your noses this whole time.
那女人的动作不像普通客人。她一直替某个人盯着会客室。
That woman did not behave like an ordinary guest. She was watching the parlor for someone.
如果她真是 Whale 的耳目，这案子就不是酒吧里的人自己能收拾的。
If she truly works for Whale, this is not something anyone inside the club can contain.
事实我说完了。别再问我站在哪一边。
Those are the facts. Do not ask me whose side I am on.
别拿“算账”糊弄我。Webb 后来找的接班人，是不是也替他跑这些脏活？
Do not hide behind "doing the books." Did Webb's successor run the same dirty errands for him?
跑腿的活儿，酒吧里不少人都碰过。真正的脏活，只交给身份不干净的人。
Plenty of people in the club ran ordinary errands. The truly dirty work went only to people with questionable papers.
因为他们需要 Webb 手里的合法身份。
Because they needed the legal identities Webb could provide.
对。我以前也是其中一个。
Yes. I used to be one of them.
我知道那摊脏活有多深，也知道拿到那张纸以后，人会有多怕失去它。
I know how deep that filth runs, and how afraid a person becomes of losing those papers once they have them.
后来接手的人，就是 Webb 新拴住的那条线。
Whoever took over after me was simply the next person Webb put on a leash.
那个人是谁？
Who was it?
我不知道名字。Webb 不会把所有线都交给一个账房。
I don't know the name. Webb would never place every line in the hands of one bookkeeper.
但你能确定，真有这么一个接班人。
But you are certain there really was a successor.
确定。Webb 手里的合法身份，就是拴人的绳子。去找那个最怕失去那张纸的人。
I am. The legal identities in Webb's hands were leashes. Find the person most afraid of losing those papers.
这已经是我能说的全部。
That is everything I can tell you.
行，我会查。
All right. I'll look into it.
看看这枚案发现场的弹壳。是不是让你想起了点旧伤？
Take a look at this casing from the crime scene. Does it remind you of an old wound?
……您从哪儿找到这东西的。
...Where did you find that thing.
你之前这儿的弹壳，也是这个口径吧？
The casing that hit you back then... same caliber, right?
.45……这可是时下常用的配枪口径。
.45... that's the standard sidearm caliber these days.
就像外面那个 Morrison 侦探腰里别的那把……
Like the one Detective Morrison carries on his hip out there...
或者是你们这片区会用的那把。
...or the kind they use around this neighborhood.
弹壳？什么弹壳？当时差点丢了命之后，我就学乖了，只坐在屋里算账。
Casings? What casings? After I nearly died that time, I learned my lesson — I just sit in my room and do the books.
外头的烂活儿，枪，子弹，我是没碰。
The dirty work outside — the guns, the bullets — I haven't touched any of it.
对我来说……活着比什么都强。所以，Webb先生才找了个接班人。
For me... staying alive beats everything else. That's why Mr. Webb found someone to take my place.
他选接班人有什么标准？
What was his criteria for picking a replacement?
这片儿能干这种活的，多半都是……身份不大干净的人。
The kind of people who can do this work around here... they're mostly folks whose papers aren't exactly... clean.
Webb先生有渠道，能把艾斯弗德的合法身份递到他们手上。
Mr. Webb had the connections to get them legitimate Ashford identity papers.
您要问标准——大概就是，谁更想要那张纸。
You ask about criteria? I'd say... whoever wanted that piece of paper the most.
那你呢？你拿到合法身份了吗？
And you? Did you get your papers?
Webb先生守过他对我的承诺。剩下的话，您自己想吧。
Mr. Webb kept his promise to me. ...You can draw your own conclusions from that.
行了。就问到这儿。
All right. That's enough for now.
账目我这儿一直开着，Brennan 先生。您有什么要查的，随时来。
The books are always open, Mr. Brennan. Anything you need to check... come by anytime.
没有其他问题了。
No more questions.
等等。你抽屉里也藏着一枚弹壳。
Hold it. You have a casing hidden in this drawer too.
比Rosa交出的那枚旧得多，可底印是同一套 .45 警用规格。
Older than the one Rosa handed over, but it carries the same .45 police-pattern headstamp.
把抽屉关上，Brennan。那不是你的证物。
Close the drawer, Brennan. That is not your evidence.
同样的底印。你跟案发那把枪，是什么关系？
Same headstamp. What is your connection to the gun used in the murder?
几年前的旧账。跟Webb今晚的死没有半点关系。
An old debt from years ago. It has nothing to do with Webb’s death tonight.
想活着，就别在这间屋里追问。
If you want to stay alive, stop asking about it in this room.
行。可这笔旧账，我记下了。
Fine. But I am writing down that old debt.
